action_semantics.representation: absolute joint-position target in motor degrees, six arm joints plus gripper
action_semantics.stored_value: values returned by robot.send_action after direction/scale mapping, joint-limit clipping and relative target capping
action_semantics.no_command_frame: applied target is copied forward unchanged; command timestamp stays empty
action_semantics.initialization: measured state initializes applied once when the control session starts, not on every R/start-recording event
action_semantics.next_episode: saved episodes within one app session inherit the last applied target; the initial target need not equal that episode's first measured state
action_semantics.deployment_conversion: driver_input[j] = predicted_motor_target_deg[j] / joint_directions[j]; send_action multiplies by those factors again
action_semantics.gripper_keys: o requests measured gripper angle minus 8 degrees; p requests plus 8 degrees, then driver limits apply

row_order: read image and record camera receive timestamp
read measured motor state and record feedback-read completion
compute and send new target if goal changes
save returned target and command-send completion timestamp
record image, measured pre-command state, applied target and timing row
training_alignment: Keep the original within-row observation-before-action convention. Do not shift stored targets solely to reduce actuator tracking lag. Keep held-target frames.

source_anchors.meaning: session target initialized from measured state
camera read followed by measured feedback
hold last applied target by default
gripper increment computed from measured motor angle
inverse direction scaling, send and store returned applied target
episode creation/saving does not reinitialize the session target
record pre-command state with post-dispatch applied target
feedback radians converted to motor degrees
return mapped and limited motor-degree target

limits_of_verification: The source commit used during the November 12 recordings is not embedded in the archive. This review verifies the source now supplied and its consistency with recorded logs, not byte-identical historical collection code.
Command completion timestamps show software dispatch completion, not hardware execution acknowledgement.
Camera timestamps are receive times, not exposure times. Per-motor feedback ages and synchronized sample timestamps were not recorded.
Hardware-free tests use a mock robot; no device or macOS GUI was exercised.
